newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Lloyds TSB shares to run to 560p.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Lloyds TSB shares to run to 560p.

text.p: DAY'S RANGE * SUPPORT * RESTNCE* MA-25 * MA-200
+ Lloyds TSB shares may break higher towards 560p initially and then to 600p longer-term, technical analysts said.
+ The shares are currently consolidating within a symmetrical triangle pattern and an upward break from this will signal the stock's uptrend since June 1996 can continue.
+ A longer consolidation period should allow the stock's 25 and 200 day moving averages to lessen their divergence.
Shares in banking group Lloyds TSB may stall over the short-term but they have the potential to go higher longer-term, technical analysts said on Monday.

"The shares are close to breaking out of a well constructed triangle formation extending back to mid-February, opening the way for further progress to the 560p level," said Richard Marshall, a director at Investment Research of Cambridge Ltd.
"The shares look capable of moving on to our target at 600p from this position (longer-term)," he added.
By 1050 GMT, Lloyds TSB shares were up 1-1/2p to 516-1/2p.

The shares are currently describing a symmetrical triangle pattern -- which consists of a pair of converging trendlines that connect the peaks and troughs of the share price chart -- and is usually regarded as a continuation chart pattern representing a pause in the existing trend.

Marshall expects resolution of the current consolidation phase for Lloyds TSB to be an upward break for the share price which will continue the stock's uptrend since June 1996 when it took off from a low of 305p.
Its share price strength has meant that Lloyds TSB has outperformed the All-Share index by about 52 percent since June.
This compares well against the banks sector which has notched up a 34 percent outperformance against the All-Share index over the same period.
"The price pattern (for Lloyds TSB) remains one of the strongest of the UK banks," said Marshall.

But he noted that divergence between Lloyds TSB's 25 and 200 day moving averages is now approaching a hefty 28 percent and needs to shrink a little over the near-term, perhaps as a result of consolidation, before the shares can run up to his 600p target.
